name: Kanchenjunga Expedition
sub_region: Taplejung District, Koshi Province (Kangchenjunga Himal; Kanchenjunga Conservation Area; Nepal-Sikkim/India border)

difficulty.notes: Third-highest mountain. Standard Nepal commercial line is the Southwest Face from the Yalung Glacier (1955 British route): glacier and serac terrain, then steep snow/ice to a high camp on the Gangway, then mixed ground to the summit pyramid. North-side routes from Pangpema exist but are not the usual commercial product. Remote; fewer teams than Everest or Manaslu. Operators ask for prior 7,000 m experience. Supplemental oxygen is normal on commercial summit days.

duration_days.notes: Seven Summit Treks lists 50 days (Bhadrapur-Phidim-Yamphudin-Tseram, helicopter Tseram-Base Camp, ~1 month of rotations, helicopter out). Fully walked approaches without helicopter are longer. Asian Hiking Team lists 54-day fixed dates.

max_altitude_point: Kangchenjunga Main (Kangchenjunga I). Subsidiary summits include Yalung Kang / West 8,505 m and South 8,494 m (SST list; not independently re-surveyed here)
start_point: Bhadrapur (flight from Kathmandu) then drive Phidim / Yamphudin

itinerary.route: Arrive Kathmandu; DoT briefing, restricted-area and climbing permits, gear check
itinerary.notes: RAP must be issued in Kathmandu through a registered agency.

itinerary.route: Fly Kathmandu - Bhadrapur; drive to Phidim

itinerary.notes: Restricted-area checkpost. Some itineraries still jeep only as far as Taplejung and walk from Chiruwa.
South-side trail of the Kanchenjunga Base Camp trek.

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation at Tseram; hike toward Ramche (about 4,580 m) / Oktang
Tseram - Kanchenjunga South / Yalung Base Camp (helicopter on the SST programme; otherwise trek via Ramche-Oktang and the Yalung Glacier moraine)
itinerary.notes: SST Advance Base Camp 5,475 m. Other operators give 5,400-5,500 m.

itinerary.route: Puja and rotations on the Yalung Glacier SW Face: Camp 1 (about 6,200 m) - Camp 2 (about 6,400 m) - Camp 3 (about 7,100 m) - return to Base Camp
itinerary.walking_hours: C1 4-5 h; C1-C2 2-3 h; C2-C3 about 5 h (SST)
itinerary.notes: Camp positions move with crevasses and snow.

itinerary.route: Summit window: Camp 4 (about 7,550-7,570 m) - summit 8,586 m - descend to Camp 3 or 2 - Base Camp
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day about 9-10 h from Camp 4; 5-6 h down (SST)
itinerary.notes: Late-night start; summit typically 8-10 am. 1955 first-ascent party stopped a few feet short of the summit cone at Sikkimese request; modern commercial teams generally go to the surveyed summit - treat current practice as operator-dependent.

itinerary.route: Helicopter Base Camp - Tapetok (SST) or trek out; drive Phidim - Bhadrapur; fly Kathmandu

best_seasons.notes: Spring is the primary commercial season. Autumn is offered but with less infrastructure. Winter is specialist only. Royalty is higher in spring (USD 3,000) than autumn (USD 1,500).

permits.name: Department of Tourism climbing royalty - other mountains above 8,000 m (includes Kanchenjunga)
permits.fee: USD 3,000 per person spring; USD 1,500 autumn; USD 750 winter/summer

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per team) - peaks above 8,000 m, other ranges
Kanchenjunga Restricted Area Permit (Taplejung: Phaktanglung wards 6-7, Mikwakhola ward 5, Sirijunga ward 8)
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week for the first 4 weeks; USD 25 per week beyond. Immigration has stated expedition-permit holders must obtain the RAP but do not pay its fee.
permits.status: VERIFIED (fee table); climber fee-waiver UNVERIFIED on a live Immigration page in this research

permits.name: TIMS card (agency-issued) on the approach trek
permits.fee: NPR 2,000 (SAARC NPR 1,000). Whether mountaineering-permit holders are also charged TIMS is UNVERIFIED (TAAN has said TIMS is not required for climbers holding mountaineering permits).
permits.applies_to: foreign trekkers on Kanchenjunga routes listed by NTB

guide_requirements: Restricted area: licensed guide, registered agency; since 22 March 2026 solo trekkers may obtain RAP (two-person minimum removed), max 7 trekkers per guide. On the mountain: Sixth Amendment solo ban on 8,000 m peaks; at least one mountain guide or high-altitude worker per two members; liaison officer; staff insurance minimums. SST south-side programmes budget 1 climbing Sherpa per member on summit day (operator practice, not the legal minimum).

flights: Helicopter Tseram - Base Camp and return on some commercial programmes
logistics.notes: Lodges to Tseram; tented Base Camp on Yalung moraine for about a month. Fully walked south approaches may still camp above Yamphudin in shoulder seasons. No Khumbu Icefall / SPCC Icefall fee.

highlights: Yalung Glacier and southwest face, the 1955 first-ascent line
Remote eastern Nepal; Kanchenjunga Conservation Area

First ascent 25 May 1955: George Band and Joe Brown (expedition led by Charles Evans); Norman Hardie and Tony Streather on 26 May. The 1955 party stopped short of standing on the summit snow in deference to Sikkimese religious requests
risks: Avalanche and serac hazard on the SW Face / Yalung Glacier
Extreme altitude and a long summit day from Camp 4
Long road transfers on the Bhadrapur-Phidim axis

acclimatization.notes: SST rotation block is days 11-35 before a days 36-45 summit window. Walk-in teams add the lower-valley days as extra acclimatisation.

unverified: Subsidiary-peak heights on the SST page (West 8,505 m, South 8,494 m) not cross-checked against Himalayan Database in this pass.
Whether 2026 commercial teams stand on the true summit or stop short (1955 practice).
RAP fee waiver for expedition-permit holders: used in 2026-10-20 regulations research; Immigration trekking-permit URL returned 404 on 2026-10-22.
KCA SAARC rate (trek file cites NPR 500; _regulations.json leaves SAARC null — foreign NPR 2,000 used).
